meta.scope: Bolivia batch 2 — External sector (BOP, trade), hydrocarbons decline, minerals boom, soy/agro, and departmental poverty contrast. Begins the lived-economy picture.

candidates.title: Balanza de Pagos / Balance of Payments
candidates.description: Quarterly and annual balance of payments covering the current account, capital/financial account and changes in reserve assets.
candidates.notes: Core external-accounts product. Current-account outcomes have been under pressure as gas exports decline; recent periods show mixed results driven by mineral prices and remittances.

candidates.title: Estadísticas de Comercio Exterior / Merchandise Trade
candidates.description: Monthly and annual statistics of exports and imports of goods. Export basket dominated by minerals (gold, silver, zinc, tin), hydrocarbons (gas), and non-traditional agro-products (soy derivatives, beef, Brazil nuts).
candidates.notes: Primary high-frequency trade product. 2025 exports ~USD 9.6 bn. Minerals have overtaken hydrocarbons as the leading export category after the structural decline in gas production and the end of the Argentina gas contract.

candidates.title: Gas natural — producción y exportaciones
candidates.description: Statistics of natural-gas production and exports. Historically the dominant export and fiscal-revenue source; now in structural decline.
candidates.notes: Structural turning point. Gas exports fell ~34% in value in 2025; the Argentina contract ended in 2024 and volumes to Brazil have declined. Once the backbone of the fiscal and external accounts; now a diminishing pillar.

candidates.title: Minerales — oro, plata, zinc, estaño
candidates.description: Statistics of mineral production and exports (gold, silver, zinc, tin and others). Now the leading merchandise-export category by value.
candidates.notes: Current export engine. 2025 mineral exports ~USD 5.6 bn (+26%), driven by gold and silver prices. Replaces gas as the primary external-revenue source in the short term.

candidates.title: Soya y derivados — producción y exportaciones
candidates.description: Statistics of soybean and soybean-product production and exports. Leading non-traditional agro-export, concentrated in the eastern lowlands (Santa Cruz).
candidates.notes: Key non-traditional export. Complements the mineral and (declining) hydrocarbon pillars; production and export geography is heavily Santa Cruz–centred.

candidates.title: Departamento de Santa Cruz — low-poverty economic hub
candidates.description: Eastern lowland department and the country’s main agro-industrial and commercial engine. Lowest departmental poverty incidence.
candidates.notes: Economic counterweight to the highland departments. Poverty incidence among the lowest in the country (~20–25% range in recent readings); hosts the bulk of soy, beef and related agro-industry.

candidates.title: Departamento de Potosí — high-poverty highland contrast
candidates.description: Highland mining department with among the highest poverty and extreme-poverty incidence.
candidates.notes: Poverty-contrast department. Frequently ranks near the top of departmental poverty (mid-to-high 40s–50s % in recent years) despite its historic and ongoing mining role.

candidates.title: Departamento de Chuquisaca — high-poverty contrast
candidates.description: Southern highland/valley department with elevated poverty incidence.
candidates.notes: Completes the high-poverty highland set alongside Potosí. Poverty incidence often above 50% in recent readings.

candidates.title: Departamento de La Paz — capital region
candidates.description: Western highland department containing the seat of government (La Paz) and El Alto. Intermediate-to-higher poverty and the largest absolute number of people in poverty.
candidates.notes: Demographic and political core. Large absolute poverty mass even when rates are not the highest; hosts the dual-city complex of La Paz and El Alto.

candidates.title: Pobreza monetaria por departamento (INE)
candidates.description: Official departmental tabulations of monetary poverty. Primary source for the inter-departmental poverty gradient.
candidates.notes: Key homogeneity-test product. Clear pattern: highland departments (Potosí, Chuquisaca, parts of La Paz) carry the highest rates; Santa Cruz the lowest. Absolute poverty is concentrated in the three largest departments (La Paz, Santa Cruz, Cochabamba).

proposed_edges.basis: Balance of payments is compiled by the Banco Central de Bolivia.
Merchandise trade flows are a primary input into the goods account of the balance of payments.
Natural gas remains a material (though declining) export line.
Minerals are now the leading merchandise-export category by value.
Soy and derivatives are the leading non-traditional agro-export.
Departmental poverty tables are geographic disaggregations of the national monetary-poverty measurement.
Santa Cruz is the principal production and export base for soy and related agro-industry.
Potosí’s high poverty ranking is derived from the departmental poverty tabulations.
